Crypto Market Analysis

14 assets · 2019-01-01 → 2026-09-30 · evaluation window from 2020-12-31 · source: synthetic regime-switching market (seed 7)

Synthetic data. This report was generated from the built-in simulated market so the pipeline can run offline. Numbers illustrate the method and are not market results. Run python -m cryptolab report --source binance for live data.

Key findings

Generated automatically from the analysis below.

  • Highest risk-adjusted return over the evaluation window: Regime-gated EW (WF) (Sharpe 0.79, max drawdown -77%).
  • Best of 18 momentum configurations had Sharpe 0.91. Deflated for the number of trials (luck alone would be expected to reach ≈ 0.20), the probability its true Sharpe is above zero is 97%. Equal-weight buy-and-hold alone scored 0.75 on the same sample, so much of that is market exposure rather than selection skill.
  • Walk-forward selection chose 3 different lookbacks across 24 folds; out-of-sample Sharpe 0.77 vs. 0.91 for the hindsight-optimal setting.
  • Market regime now: bull / calm (P(bull) = 100%). 8 of 14 assets carry a positive composite signal.
  • Average correlation with BTC is 0.86 on all days and 0.85 on BTC's worst 10% of days; with correlations this high, spreading capital across coins diversifies little.
  • Doubling trading costs to 30 bps hurts XS momentum (WF) most (Sharpe 0.77 → 0.71), in line with its turnover of 26× a year.
  • Vectorised indicator engine computes the full indicator set for 14 assets (37,753 rows) in 76 ms, 5.0× faster than a loop implementation (80% less compute time).

3 · Is any of this real? Statistical controls

A backtest Sharpe ratio is a noisy estimate, and the best of many tried configurations is biased upwards. The table gives stationary-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (blocks preserve volatility clustering), the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio (adjusted for skew and fat tails) and the track record needed for 95% confidence. The heatmap shows all 18 momentum configurations tested; the Deflated Sharpe Ratio in the key findings accounts for every one of them.

4 · Market regimes

A two-state Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (Baum-Welch EM, written from scratch in NumPy) on BTC's 10-day mean return and log 20-day volatility. It is refitted every 90 days on past data only, and the shading uses the forward-filtered probability, which never sees the future. Parameters below are from the latest fit.

6 · Indicator panel

7 · Methodology and limitations

  • No look-ahead. Every indicator and signal is unit-tested by scrambling all data after a cut-off and asserting that values before it do not change. The backtester applies day-t weights to day t+1 returns.
  • Costs and drift. Turnover is measured against weights after they drift with prices, so costs are not understated. Rebalancing is weekly with a 1% no-trade band.
  • Survivorship bias. The universe is today's large caps. Coins that collapsed (e.g. LUNA, FTT) are absent, which flatters any long-only crypto result.
  • Not modelled: funding rates and shorting, exchange outages, tax, capacity and market impact beyond a flat slippage charge.
  • Sample size. Crypto has had only a few full market cycles; the wide Sharpe confidence intervals reflect that.
